selected_sources.body:
### Issue for this PR

No separate tracking issue. Related context work: [#46574](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/46574) and [#53080](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/53080). Targets `v2`, matching this implementation's architecture.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [x] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Gateway users currently need local model definitions to expose model limits and capabilities. This adds opt-in discovery through `providers.<id>.settings.modelDiscovery`, using the configured provider URL, existing API-key connection or environment credentials, and headers. No per-model definitions or renamed model aliases are required. OpenCode contacts only the configured gateway.

The optional OpenAI-style `/models` extension carries independent total-context, input and output limits, API endpoints, tools/parallel tools, exact reasoning choices/defaults, input/output modalities, and chosen output-request defaults. These are documented extension fields, not additions to the standard OpenAI model-list contract. Any compatible gateway can implement them; this client change has no LiteLLM dependency. [LiteLLM #45023](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/45023) provides the companion catalog, metadata and serving policy; it is independently useful to HTTP clients and does not need to merge before this PR. Gateways returning only IDs can still provide discovered models, with ordinary compatibility behavior for missing metadata.

A successful catalog is authoritative for that opted-in provider, including an empty catalog. Removed models are unavailable for new parent/subagent requests even with local metadata overrides; reappearing models regain current metadata. In-flight requests retain their snapshot, and unrelated providers retain existing behavior. Failed/malformed polls retain the last valid catalog. Configuration/credential changes invalidate account-scoped metadata; source and refresh-generation guards reject stale concurrent results. Invalid IDs, duplicates and negative limits reject the complete response.

Discovery metadata overrides existing catalog defaults field by field; explicit local metadata remains authoritative for listed models. Advertised Responses is preferred over Chat Completions unless an explicit package overrides the choice. Reasoning choices become variants of the same model ID.

Optional `request_defaults` output budgets, including budgets by reasoning effort, are distinct from supplier output maxima. Local `settings.outputTokenBudget` overrides them; known maxima still constrain requests. The effective budget governs normal generation and advance compaction reservation for both parents and subagents. Compaction respects independent input limits and total context after output reservation, preserving the existing estimation buffer. Unknown limits stay unknown.

Initial model reads await plugin activation and one bounded account/configuration-scoped discovery attempt. API-key login waits for that attempt before reporting Connected, and the first read after a cold restart sees the catalog. Failed attempts preserve saved credentials and ordinary providers, log a sanitized warning, and retry periodically.

Public client types were regenerated. `specs/v2/model-discovery.md` documents configuration, the vendor-neutral wire extension, inventory semantics and budget precedence. This PR is independently useful with any implementing gateway; a corresponding LiteLLM producer change supplies one tested implementation but is not required to merge this client.

### How did you verify your code works?

Reproducible repository checks (run tests from their package directories):

```sh
(cd packages/schema && bun test test/model.test.ts test/contract-hygiene.test.ts)
(cd packages/server && bun test test/model.test.ts)
(cd packages/ai && bun test test/provider/openai-chat.test.ts test/provider/openai-compatible-chat.test.ts)
(cd packages/client && bun run generate)
(cd packages/cli && bun run build --single --skip-install --skip-web-ui)
```

The upstream API-key metadata/request-body fix and Azure credential configuration regressions are included. Public client generation produced no tracked delta, and the Linux CLI built successfully. Compiled isolated API and PTY login fixtures passed immediate/cold-first catalog reads and default reads; authenticated discovery completed before Connected, with zero inference.

selected_sources.body:
With compaction.inContext enabled, compaction can generate the summary inside the cached conversation: it repeats the request the next turn would send, appends the instructions as a system message plus a user message, and sets toolChoice none. The recent tail is kept as before. A gate requires a verified model, a warm cache from the same model and thinking level, room in the context window, and a lower estimated cost than the standalone summary. Failed or rejected attempts fall back to the standalone summary, never execute tools, and are recorded in details.inContext with their usage.

pi-ai adds the supportsInContextCompaction compat setting and test/in-context-compaction-probe.ts, which measures whether a model keeps its prompt cache for this request shape. The generated catalog flags the models that passed.

selected_sources.title: fix(ai): honor Retry-After delays in agent-level retry
selected_sources.body:
Fixes #10601. (Same gap as #9595, which was bot-closed before review.)

Problem: agent-level auto-retry ignores the server's `Retry-After` / `retry-after-ms`. A 429 with `Retry-After: 30` is retried after 2s and then on `2^(n-1)` backoff — earlier than the server asked — hammering a rate-limited or overloaded backend.

Trace: each API catch block flattens the provider error to a display string (`formatProviderError(normalizeProviderError(error))`), `normalizeProviderError` never reads response headers, and `AssistantMessage` has no field to carry them, so `retryDelayMs()` can only use the exponential formula. Provider-level `retryProviderRequest` parses the headers but is off by default (`settings.retry.provider.maxRetries = 0`) because it delays pi's own quota/usage-limit handling.

Solution:

- `parseRetryAfterMs(headers)`: extracted from `getRetryDelayMs` and shared. Provider-path behavior unchanged, including the malformed-date fallback (#9571).
- `extractRetryAfterMs(error)`: reads the hint from SDK errors carrying response `Headers`; every chat API error path now sets `AssistantMessage.retryAfterMs`.
- `retryDelayMs(policy, attempt, serverDelayMs)`: raises the per-attempt delay to the hint. `maxAgentDelayMs` stays authoritative: the hint is clamped to the cap and never lowers the exponential delay.
- Consumers: `retryAssistantCall`, `AgentSession._prepareRetry`, and the durable harness generation/compaction schedulers.

Tests: regression tests beside the retry suites (commented `#9595`) plus unit tests for `parseRetryAfterMs` and `extractRetryAfterMs`. `npm run check` is clean. `./test.sh` passes except two Windows-shell tests (`resolve-config-value` "uses stdin when the configured Windows shell requires it", `env-node` "uses stdin command transport for legacy WSL bash paths") that fail identically on unmodified main in my Linux environment.

selected_sources.title: fix(ai): defer streamed tool argument parsing until read
selected_sources.body:
fixes #9265

Stops reparsing the full accumulated tool-call json on every delta. Instead moves reparsing into per-access of `.arguments` (cached, so only first access on same version re-parses).

---

It isn't complex code but it's not idiomatic in the codebase and **I'm not sure it's worth it**. It's done this way not to break anyone existing (mostly at least), but maybe making the system explicit in removing this field access and adding getter method instead (to indicate potential ad-hoc work) s.a. `getLastSnapshot()` would be better. (It'll allow cleanup of some copy shenanigans which try to copy objects without triggering field reads. ).

I chose not to do it not to break folks but with AI and changelogs and how pi approaches braking changes maybe it'd be better. Let me know or just change my PR / use it as base for your fix. Whichever works.

---

In any case, this removes unconditional whole-prefix argument parsing from the seven ingestion paths we identified. Reasoning-signature accumulation was already fixed, and plain text/thinking ingestion only appends deltas. It doesn't address frame-encoder catch-up, which can still reparse growing prefixes.

**Do note:** The current TUI still reads arguments on each update, so it can still incur quadratic parsing, this PR just makes it so other more conscious consumers don't have to.

---

 A few visible differences: the proxy now ignores argument deltas after toolcall_end instead of letting alte data override them. Some other malformed event sequences (s.a. pi-messages argument deltas after tool end) can now error where main tolerated them. Live .arguments is also a getter/setter, so strict descriptor-based validators like isJsonValue() can reject it even though normal field access and JSON serialization work.
